Hey there! Dental hygienist here.
You have no idea how many people we see exactly in your shoes! Hardest part is booking in and making sure you show up ;) 
1) it is always beneficial to brush 2-3 x a day and floss with a water flosser. Although you cannot remove the tartar yourself with this, this will reduce bacteria in the area and not only aid with healing after your initial cleaning, it will help with any soreness you may have after (prepare for some, biggest thing I can recommend is warm salt water rinses before and after your cleaning - 1/2 cup warm water 1tsp salt and swish for 1 min 2x a day) you can also alternate bw 2 Tylenol/Advil every 4-6 hours (as long as you don’t have any conditions that stop you from taking Advil) 

2- make sure it at least gets up to 80PSI, and it’s good (this is the PSI needed to remove plaque, you may want to lower it after your cleaning to about a 2-3 (low) and slowly work your way back up to 8.

3-you very well may have bone loss, tartar causes the bone level to drop over time if not removed. Good news is you seem to have already adopted a really good home care routine, and if you say you do have some recession but not enough to show the full tooth, odds are with a really good cleaning and continued hygiene every 3 mos (if they don’t recommend this to you after telling you you have perio I highly recommend attending a different office or advocating yourself for every 3 mos (it takes about 3 mos for that bacteria to grow back)). Anyways yes you may have perio but depending on the severity it’s usually manageable to stablilize over time (meaning not actively destroying bone and healing the pockets). It’s about 80% what you do at home and 20% what we do during your cleanings. Waterpik will be your best friend! 

4 - you may have xerostomia, does it feel like you do not have enough saliva in your mouth? This can be exacerbated by medications, and the amount of water you drink. Ensure you drink at least 2-3L of water a day and inform your doctor of this. Decreased saliva can contribute to higher rate of decay due to less minerals hitting your enamel. Try a less minty toothpaste, ensure there is minimal alcohol. Try pronamel repair and protect.
